description: A bare `return` engine message arm is grammatical under §18.2 `leave-stmt` but illegal by context — a message arm is no function body: E-STMT-RETURN-OUTSIDE-FUNCTION (dpa-068 c14 / D10).
rationale: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S462 "2 W1" — §18.2 `arm-body ::= expression | block-body | leave-stmt`; `leave-stmt ::= 'return' expression? | 'fail' variant-expr | 'break' Label? | 'continue' Label?`, arms only (match arms in statement, decl and value position, `!{}` handler arms, engine message arms); legality by context (§7). A bare leave arm means what the braced one-statement block means: `return` / `fail` leave the enclosing function (§19.3.3), `break` / `continue` the enclosing loop (§19.4.3). A message arm keeps refusing `return` with the real legality code.
